title.en: Read all records from a binary file

say.en: A text file stores only strings. What if you want to save a list like [1, "Asha", 30000] and get back a list, not text? pickle does that. In this lesson: Explain serialization and deserialization.
Use pickle.dump() and pickle.load().
Read all records from a binary file.

body.en: The pickle module converts a Python object (list, dictionary, tuple…) into a byte stream that can be stored in a binary file; this is *pickling* or serialization. Converting the byte stream back into the same object is unpickling or deserialization. dump(data_object, file_object) writes an object to a file opened in binary write mode, and load(file_object) reads the next object from a file opened in binary read mode.

load() raises EOFError at the end of the file

myth.en: I can open the pickle file with open("students.dat", "w") and dump into it, like a text file.

truth.en: pickle writes bytes, so the file must be opened in binary mode: "wb", "ab" or "rb". With "w", pickle.dump() raises a TypeError. Both are "files", so text mode seems fine. A text-mode file object accepts only str, while dump produces bytes.

say.en: pickle stores Python objects in binary files: dump(obj, f) writes, load(f) reads.
Use binary modes only: wb, ab, rb (and rb+, wb+, ab+).
Read to the end with while True inside try, stopped by except EOFError.
Update = read all records, change the match, write all back with wb.
Append new records with ab so old records are kept.

narration.en: Many people think: I can open the pickle file with open("students.dat", "w") and dump into it, like a text file. Actually: pickle writes bytes, so the file must be opened in binary mode: "wb", "ab" or "rb". With "w", pickle.dump() raises a TypeError. Both are "files", so text mode seems fine. A text-mode file object accepts only str, while dump produces bytes.

problem.en: Store two employee records in a binary file and display them. Give the exact output.

narration.en: Each dump writes one record. The loop keeps loading until load() raises EOFError, which we catch to stop cleanly.

say.en: Each dump writes one record. The loop keeps loading until load() raises EOFError, which we catch to stop cleanly. Store two employee records in a binary file and display them. Give the exact output.
import pickle.
with open("emp.dat", "wb") as f.
for rec in records.
pickle.dump(rec, f).
with open("emp.dat", "rb") as f.
try.
while True.
print(pickle.loadf).
except EOFError.
print("End of file").

So the answer is [1, 'Asha', 30000]
[2, 'Ravi', 25000]
End of file.
